paragraphs: Elovate sells automated traffic enforcement programs to communities that want fewer crashes on their streets. State and local agencies are the buyers, and the company frames the work as helping them improve road safety. Four turnkey programs run on one platform, shaped around streets, work zones and school corridors.

Cameras capture speeding and red-light running events for enforcement. Agencies then handle citations from issuance through resolution in the violation processing software. A product called CiteWeb keeps a chain of custody and an audit trail for every citation. Reporting tools track trends and identify high-need areas so deployment can be adjusted. The company also works with municipalities on outreach campaigns about a program's fairness and transparency.

Elovate says it has partnered with municipalities across the United States for more than 30 years. It dates its camera enforcement at signalized intersections back to 1997. Its work zone speed enforcement runs programs in six states today.
